newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain to close mining firm Hunosa in 2002 - report.
newsitem.headline: Spain to close mining firm Hunosa in 2002 - report.

text.p: Spain's Industry Minister Josep Pique has announced the government will stop subsidising state-owned coal mining firm Hunosa in 2002, in practice closing the company down, the Spanish daily El Pais said on Saturday.
"(There will be) an ambitious reconversion plan for the modernisation and liberalisation of the coal mine," Pique was reported as saying.

The government's current plan guaranteeing public funds ends in December 1997. Pique said he wanted to negotiate the reconversion plan with unions and regional governments, which sharply criticised the move to shut down the mining company.
The minister plans to reduce production and capacity to limit them to the most profitable areas.
The conservative government's draft 1997 budget does not set aside a sum for public sector subsidies and instead aims to pay them out of privatisation profits and through loans.

Pique in August said the government would set aside 100 billion pesetas for the mining industry between 1997 and 1999, of which 60 to 70 billion would go towards the region of Asturias where Hunosa is based, according to El Pais.
Hunosa currently employs 9,300 people and is expected to lose around 45 billion pesetas this year, the newspaper said.
